title: Every notification the application sends records an outcome on a durable sink that operators can query by recipient and window
description: The application records the outcome of every notification it attempts to send (email, SMS, push, webhook, or any other channel the project ships) as a structured record on a durable outcome sink. Each record carries a notification identifier, a channel name from a fixed enum, a recipient identifier, an outcome from a fixed enum (delivered, failed, pending, suppressed), an attemptedAt ISO-8601 timestamp, and an optional errorCode string when the outcome is failed. An operator queries the sink by recipient identifier and time window and receives the outcome records that match. Notifications never succeed silently: an attempt with no recorded outcome is a defect the project must gate against.
rationale: A silent notification channel is the shape that produces 'the customer says they never got the email' with no way to distinguish 'we never sent it' from 'the provider dropped it' from 'the recipient filtered it'. The outcome record is what turns that question into a query. The suppressed outcome value covers the case where an active incident notice suppresses noisy notifications; the record still lands so the operator can audit the suppression later.
